translations.literal: Reaching Tumen Army, he entered the bathhouse, suffered a wind ailment, collapsed unconscious for a long while before reviving.
translations.idiomatic: At Tumen garrison he entered the bathhouse, suffered a stroke, and collapsed for a long while before reviving.

sentences.zh: 因入京，廢疾於家。

translations.literal: He therefore entered the capital and was disabled by illness at home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital and was disabled by illness at home.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，上以封常清、高仙芝喪敗，召翰入，拜為皇太子先鋒兵馬元帥，以田良丘為御史中丞，充行軍司馬，以王思禮、鉗耳大福、李承光、蘇法鼎、管崇嗣及蕃將火拔歸仁、李武定、渾萼、契苾寧等為裨將，河隴、朔方兵及蕃兵與高仙芝舊卒共二十萬，拒賊於潼關。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, because Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated and lost, the emperor summoned Han and appointed him Vanguard Commander of the Heir Apparent's Army; Tian Liangqiu was made Censor-in-Chief and Campaigning Major; Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and barbarian generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, Qibi Ning, and others were made deputy generals — Hexi, Longyou, Shuofang troops and barbarian soldiers together with Gao Xianzhi's old troops, two hundred thousand in all, to resist the rebels at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, after Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi's defeats the emperor recalled Han and made him vanguard commander of the heir's army, with Tian Liangqiu as campaigning major and Wang Sili, Huoba Guiren, and others as deputies — two hundred thousand Hexi, Shuofang, and tribal troops with Xianzhi's veterans to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 上御勤政樓勞遣之，百僚出餞於郊。

translations.literal: The emperor attended at the Hall of Diligent Government to comfort and send them off; the hundred officials went out to feast them at the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw them off from the Hall of Diligent Government; the officials feasted them outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 十五載，加翰尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Han was given Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and made Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made Left Vice Director and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 翰至潼關，或勸翰曰：「祿山阻兵，以誅楊國忠為名，公若留兵三萬守關，悉以精銳回誅國忠，此漢挫七國之計也，公以為何如？」

translations.literal: When Han reached Tong Pass, someone advised him: "Lushan blocks the army and takes punishing Yang Guozhong as his pretext — if you leave thirty thousand to guard the pass and bring all your elite back to execute Guozhong, this is the Han plan for breaking the Seven States — what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass someone advised him, "Lushan marches under the banner of punishing Yang Guozhong — leave thirty thousand to hold the pass and march your best troops back to kill Guozhong, as the Han did against the Seven States — what say you?

sentences.zh: 翰心許之，未發。

translations.literal: Han agreed in his heart but did not set out.
translations.idiomatic: Han agreed in his heart but did not act.

sentences.zh: 有客泄其謀於國忠，國忠大懼，及奏曰：「兵法『安不忘危』，今潼關兵眾雖盛，而無後殿，萬一不利，京師得無恐乎！

translations.literal: A guest leaked the plan to Guozhong; Guozhong was greatly afraid and memorialized: "In military law, 'In peace do not forget danger' — now Tong Pass has a great host but no rear guard; if by chance things go ill, will not the capital be in fear!
translations.idiomatic: Someone leaked the plan to Guozhong, who in terror memorialized, "In peace forget not danger — Tong Pass is strong but has no reserve; if things go wrong, will not the capital tremble?

sentences.zh: 請選監牧小兒三千人訓練於苑中。」

translations.literal: He asked to select three thousand boys of the horse herds to train in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to train three thousand boys from the horse herds in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 詔從之，遂遣劍南軍將李福、劉光庭分統焉。

translations.literal: An edict approved this; Li Fu and Liu Guangting of the Jiannan army were then sent to command them separately.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Jiannan generals Li Fu and Liu Guangting to command them.

sentences.zh: 又奏召募一萬人，屯於灞上，令其腹心杜乾運將之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to recruit ten thousand men to encamp at Bashang, putting his confidant Du Qianyun in command.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited ten thousand men at Bashang under his confidant Du Qianyun.

sentences.zh: 翰慮為所圖，乃上表請乾運兵隸於潼關，遂召乾運赴潼關計事，因斬之。

translations.literal: Han feared he was being plotted against; he therefore memorialized asking that Qianyun's troops be placed under Tong Pass, then summoned Qianyun to Tong Pass to discuss affairs and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Han feared a plot against him, asked that Qianyun's troops be attached to Tong Pass, summoned Qianyun there on pretense of consultation, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 自是，翰心不自安。

translations.literal: From this Han's heart was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Han was uneasy.

sentences.zh: 又素有風疾，至是頗甚，軍中之務，不復躬親，委政於行軍司馬田良丘。

translations.literal: He had long had a wind ailment; by now it was quite severe — military affairs he no longer handled in person but entrusted government to Campaigning Major Tian Liangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: His old stroke had worsened; he no longer managed army affairs himself but left them to Tian Liangqiu.

sentences.zh: 良丘復不敢專斷，教令不一，頗無部伍。

translations.literal: Liangqiu in turn did not dare decide alone; orders and teachings were not unified — discipline was quite lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Liangqiu dared not decide alone; orders conflicted and discipline collapsed.

sentences.zh: 其將王思禮、李承光又爭長不葉，人無鬥志。

translations.literal: His generals Wang Sili and Li Chengguang also vied for precedence and would not cooperate — men had no fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Wang Sili and Li Chengguang vied for command and would not cooperate — the men lost heart.

sentences.zh: 先是，翰數奏祿山雖竊河朔，而不得人心，請持重以弊之，彼自離心，因而翦滅之，可不傷兵擒茲寇矣。

translations.literal: Earlier Han had repeatedly memorialized that though Lushan had seized Hebei and Shuofang he had not won men's hearts; he asked to hold firm and wear them down — they would split of themselves, and thus he could cut them off and capture this bandit without harming the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Han had repeatedly urged that though Lushan held Hebei he lacked popular support — hold the pass, wear him down, let his followers split, and destroy him without heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 賊將崔乾祐於陜郡潛鋒蓄銳，而覘者奏雲「賊殊無備」，上然之，命悉眾速討之。

translations.literal: The rebel general Cui Qianyu at Shan commandery secretly sharpened his edge and stored his strength, but scouts reported "the rebels are quite unprepared"; the emperor agreed and ordered the whole force to attack quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel general Cui Qianyu was secretly massing at Shan, but scouts reported the rebels were unprepared; the emperor believed it and ordered a full assault at once.

sentences.zh: 翰奏曰：「賊既始為AT逆，祿山久習用兵，必不肯無備，是陰計也。

translations.literal: Han memorialized: "Since the rebels have begun treason, Lushan has long practiced warfare — he will certainly not be without preparation; this is a hidden stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Han memorialized, "The rebels have risen in treason; Lushan is a veteran commander — he will not be unprepared; this is a trap.

sentences.zh: 且賊兵遠來，利在速戰。

translations.literal: Moreover the rebel troops have come from afar — their advantage lies in swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels have marched far — they need a quick fight.

sentences.zh: 今王師自戰其地，利在堅守，不利輕出；

translations.literal: Now the imperial army fights on its own ground — the advantage lies in stubborn defense, not in sallying lightly;
translations.idiomatic: Our army fights on its own ground — we should hold firm, not sally lightly;

sentences.zh: 若輕出關，是入其算。

translations.literal: if we lightly leave the pass, we enter their calculation.
translations.idiomatic: to leave the pass lightly is to fall into their trap.

sentences.zh: 乞更觀事勢。」

translations.literal: I beg to observe the situation further.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to watch the situation longer.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠恐其謀己，屢奏使出兵。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong feared Han plotted against him and repeatedly memorialized to make the army advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guozhong, fearing Han plotted against him, repeatedly urged an advance.

sentences.zh: 上久處太平，不練軍事，既為國忠眩惑，中使相繼督責。

translations.literal: The emperor had long dwelt in peace and did not practice military affairs; having been dazzled and misled by Guozhong, palace envoys came in succession to supervise and reproach.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, long at peace and unused to war, was swayed by Guozhong; palace envoys pressed Han in succession.

sentences.zh: 翰不得已，引師出關。

translations.literal: Han had no choice and led the army out of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Han had no choice and led the army out.

sentences.zh: 六月四日，次於靈寶縣之西原。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month they halted on the western plain of Lingbao county.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth of the sixth month they camped on the western plain of Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 八日，與賊交戰，官軍南迫險峭，北臨黃河；

translations.literal: On the eighth day they joined battle with the rebels; the imperial army was pressed on the south by steep peril and faced the Yellow River on the north;
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth they fought; the imperial army was pinned south against steep ground and north against the Yellow River;

sentences.zh: 崔乾祐以數千人先據險要。

translations.literal: Cui Qianyu with several thousand men had first seized the strategic heights.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qianyu had seized the heights with several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 翰及良丘浮船中流以觀進退，謂乾祐兵少，輕之，遂促將士令進，爭路擁塞，無復隊伍。

translations.literal: Han and Liangqiu floated a boat midstream to observe advance and retreat; they thought Qianyu's troops few and despised them, then urged the officers and soldiers to advance — they scrambled for the road and jammed together, with no formations left.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Liangqiu watched from a boat midstream, thought Qianyu's force small, and ordered an advance — the troops jammed the road in disorder.

sentences.zh: 午後，東風急，乾祐以草車數十乘縱火焚之，煙焰亙天。

translations.literal: In the afternoon the east wind blew hard; Qianyu set fire to several tens of hay carts — smoke and flame filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the afternoon a strong east wind rose; Qianyu fired dozens of hay carts — smoke filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 將士掩面，開目不得，因為兇徒所乘，王師自相排擠，墜於河。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers covered their faces and could not open their eyes; thus they were ridden by the fierce band — the imperial army pushed one another and fell into the river.
translations.idiomatic: The men could not see for the smoke; the rebels pressed them; the imperial troops trampled one another into the river.

sentences.zh: 其後者見前軍陷敗，悉潰，填委於河，死者數萬人，號叫之聲振天地，縛器械，以槍為楫，投北岸，十不存一二。

translations.literal: Those behind saw the front army trapped and defeated and all fled; they piled into the river — tens of thousands died; cries shook heaven and earth; binding gear and using spears as oars they cast themselves to the north bank — not one or two in ten survived.
translations.idiomatic: The rear ranks saw the van collapse and fled; tens of thousands drowned in the river, their cries shaking heaven and earth; using spears as oars they tried the north bank — fewer than one in ten survived.

sentences.zh: 軍既敗，翰與數百騎馳而西歸，為火拔歸仁執降於賊。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated, Han with several hundred cavalry galloped west to return and was seized by Huoba Guiren and surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, Han fled west with a few hundred horsemen and was seized by Huoba Guiren and surrendered to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 祿山謂之曰：「汝常輕我，今日如何？」

translations.literal: Lushan said to him: "You always looked down on me — how is it today?
translations.idiomatic: Lushan said, "You always despised me — how is it today?

sentences.zh: 翰懼，俯伏稱：「肉眼不識陛下，遂至於此。

translations.literal: Han in fear prostrated himself and said: "These fleshly eyes did not recognize Your Majesty, and thus it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Han prostrated himself in fear. "My mortal eyes failed to see Your Majesty," he said.

sentences.zh: 陛下為撥亂主，今天下未平，李光弼在土門，來填在河南，魯炅在南陽，但留臣，臣以尺書招之，不日平矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is the lord who sets chaos aright; the realm is not yet pacified — Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Tian in Henan, Lu Yong at Nanyang; only keep your servant — with a short letter your servant will summon them, and in no many days it will be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is heaven's chosen restorer; the realm is not yet settled — Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian Henan, Lu Yong Nanyang; keep me and I will summon them by letter, and peace will come in days.

sentences.zh: 祿山大喜，遂偽署翰司空。

translations.literal: Lushan was greatly pleased and thereupon falsely appointed Han Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan was delighted and made Han Minister of Works in his false court.

sentences.zh: 作書招光弼等，諸將報書皆讓翰不死節。

translations.literal: He wrote letters to summon Guangbi and the others; the generals' replies all reproached Han for not dying in honor.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to summon Guangbi and the others; every reply rebuked Han for failing to die with honor.

sentences.zh: 祿山知事不諧，遂閉翰於苑中，潛殺之。

translations.literal: Lushan knew matters would not work; he then shut Han in the park and secretly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan saw the plan would fail, imprisoned Han in the park, and had him killed in secret.

sentences.zh: 翰之守潼關也，主天下兵權，肆誌報怨，誣奏戶部尚書安思順與祿山潛通，偽令人為祿山遺思順書，於關門擒之以獻。

translations.literal: When Han guarded Tong Pass he held command of the empire's military power, indulged his will to avenge grudges, and falsely memorialized that Minister of Revenue An Sishun had secret communication with Lushan — he had someone forge a letter from Lushan to Sishun, seized him at the pass gate, and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: While holding Tong Pass Han wielded imperial military power, indulged revenge, and falsely accused Revenue Minister An Sishun of communicating with Lushan — forging a letter, seizing Sishun at the gate, and presenting him to court.

sentences.zh: 其年三月，思順及弟太仆卿元貞坐誅，徙其家屬於嶺外，天下冤之。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year Sishun and his younger brother Grand Master of the Stud Yuanzhen were executed on conviction; their families were moved beyond the Ling ranges — the realm considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: That third month Sishun and his brother Yuanzhen, Grand Master of the Stud, were executed and their families exiled beyond the Ling ranges — the realm judged it a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：大盜作梗，祿山亂常，詞雖欲誅國忠，誌則謀危社稷。

translations.literal: Commentary. The historiographer says: The great bandit raised obstruction; Lushan disturbed the norms — in words he wished to execute Guozhong, but in intent he plotted to endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary. The historiographer writes: The great rebel rose; Lushan overturned the order — he spoke of punishing Guozhong but aimed at the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 於時承平日久，金革道消，封常清、高仙芝相次率不教之兵，募市人之眾，以抗AT寇，失律喪師。

translations.literal: At that time peace had lasted long and the way of arms and armor had faded; Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi in succession led untrained troops and recruited crowds of market folk to resist the rebel band — they lost discipline and lost their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had lasted so long that warcraft had faded; Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi in turn led untrained troops and market rabble against the rebels — and lost their armies.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰廢疾於家，起專兵柄，二十萬眾拒賊關門，軍中之務不親，委任又非其所。

translations.literal: Ge Shuhan, disabled by illness at home, was raised to monopolize military power; two hundred thousand resisted the rebels at the pass gate — he did not personally handle army affairs, and those entrusted were not fit for their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Shuhan, invalid at home, was raised to sole command; two hundred thousand held the pass — yet he did not lead in person and his deputies were unfit.

sentences.zh: 及遇羯賊，旋致敗亡，天子以之播遷，自身以之拘執，此皆命帥而不得其人也。

translations.literal: When they met the Jie rebels they quickly met defeat and ruin — the Son of Heaven was driven to wander, they themselves were seized and held — all this from appointing commanders and not getting the right men.
translations.idiomatic: They met the rebels and were swiftly destroyed — the emperor fled, they were captured — all because the wrong men were given command.

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰：「大夫死眾。」

translations.literal: The Rites says: "A grandee dies for the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites says, "A grandee dies for the multitude.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「謀人之軍師敗則死之。」

translations.literal: It also says: "One who plots as another's military adviser — if defeated, dies for it."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "The strategist who fails must die."

sentences.zh: 翰受署賊庭，茍延視息，忠義之道，即可知也，豈不愧於顏杲卿乎！

translations.literal: Han accepted appointment in the rebel court and clung to life drawing breath — the way of loyalty and righteousness can be known from this; how is he not ashamed before Yan Gaoqing!
translations.idiomatic: Han took office under the rebels and clung to life — his loyalty is plain; how could he not blush before Yan Gaoqing!

sentences.zh: 抑又聞之，古之命將者，推轂而謂之曰：「閫外之事，將軍裁之。」

translations.literal: Moreover it is heard that in antiquity when appointing generals, they would push the chariot wheel and say: "Matters outside the gate — the general decides.
translations.idiomatic: We also hear that ancient emperors, appointing a general, would push the chariot wheel and say, "Beyond the gate, the general decides.

sentences.zh: 觀楊國忠之奏事，邊令誠之護戎，又掣肘於軍政者也，未可偏責三帥，不尤伊人。

translations.literal: Considering Yang Guozhong's memorials, Bian Lingcheng's supervision of the army — again hamstringing military affairs — one cannot lay all blame on the three commanders alone or reproach those men only.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yang Guozhong's interference and Bian Lingcheng's supervision — the court hamstrung its generals; one cannot blame the three commanders alone.

sentences.zh: 後之君子，得不深鑒！

translations.literal: Gentlemen of later ages — can they not take this as a deep mirror!
translations.idiomatic: Let later ages take this deeply to heart!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：羯賊犯順，戎車啟行。

translations.literal: The praise says: The Jie rebels violated obedience; war chariots set out.
translations.idiomatic: Praise runs: The Jie rebels rose in treason; war chariots rolled out.

sentences.zh: 委任失所，封、高敗亡。

translations.literal: Appointments lost their place — Feng and Gao were defeated and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Wrong men were chosen — Feng and Gao were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 虔劉圻甸，僭竊衣裳。

translations.literal: They slaughtered the capital region and usurped the imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: They ravaged the heartland and stole the imperial robes.

sentences.zh: 醜哉舒翰，不能死王。

translations.literal: Shameful is Shuhan — he could not die for his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Shame on Shuhan, who could not die for his sovereign.
